'''Kawarabuchi Shrine''' (河原淵神社, Kawarabuchi Jinja) is a {{ill|Setsumatsusha|en|Setsumatsusha|qid=Q1071160|lt=sessha}} of {{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|豊受大神宮}} ({{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|外宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Geku|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 豊受大神宮|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11633343}}) of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}}. This article also covers the former village shrine, '''Funae Kamisha''' (船江上社), located on the same grounds as Kawarabuchi Shrine.

Kamisha, and following historical research within Ise Grand Shrine after the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|en|Meiji Restoration|qid=Q8707|lt=Meiji Restoration}}, it was established on the site of Funae Kamisha.<ref name="uy0">Ujiyamada City Office (1929): vol.2, p.910</ref> The precinct of Funae Kamisha covers approximately 765 tsubo (about 2,528.9 m<sup>2</sup>), including an {{ill|Q11430523|ja|外苑|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/outer garden|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11430523}}.<ref name="uy5">Ujiyamada City Office (1929): vol.2, p.915</ref> Kawarabuchi Shrine's area is 7 are (about 694.2 m<sup>2</sup>).<ref name="uyj">Ujiyamada City Office (1929): vol.1, p.12</ref>

It Ranks 12th among the 16 sessha of Geku.<ref>Ujiyamada City Office (1929): vol.1, pp.9, 11-12</ref> Unlike most sessha, which do not have {{ill|Saisenbako|ja|賽銭箱|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/saisenbako|qid=Q135491444}} (offertory boxes), Kawarabuchi Shrine has one.<ref name="ic"/> The main shrine is surrounded by a single {{ill|Sacred fences|en|Tamagaki|qid=Q3078312|lt=tamagaki}} (fence) and features one {{ill|Torii|en|Torii|qid=Q234731|lt=torii}}.<ref name="sk">Shikinaisha Research Association (1990): p.376</ref>

The {{ill|Saijin|ja|Kami|lt=Deity}} is '''Sawahime no Mikoto''' (澤姫命),<ref name="ic"/> revered as a {{ill|Guardian deities|ja|守護神|qid=Q131278957|lt=Guardian deity}} of water.<ref name="ic"/><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.63</ref> There is speculation that the deity might be a mistaken reference to {{ill|Nakisawe|ja|鳴澤女}} in some records.<ref name="sk"/>

== Funae Kamisha ==
Funae Kamisha serves as the {{ill|Ujigami|en|Ujigami|qid=Q767655|lt=ujigami}} (guardian deity) for the local area of Funae in Ise.<ref name="ic"/><ref name="uy5"/> Its official shrine Rank under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines}} was that of a village shrine.<ref name="uy0"/> Historically known as "Hachiman-gu" by locals, it is not directly linked to {{ill|Usa Jingū|en|Usa Jingū|qid=Q715632|lt=Usa Shrine}}.<ref name="uy9">Ujiyamada City Office (1929): vol.2, p.909</ref>

Initially, the deity was either unknown or associated with {{ill|Hachiman|en|Hachiman|qid=Q261637|lt=Hachiman}}, but in 1913 (Taisho 2), it was unified with Kawarabuchi Shrine’s deity, Sawahime no Mikoto.<ref name="uy0"/> The grounds also feature various subordinate shrines.

== Oboro Pond ==
'''Oboro Pond''' (朧ヶ池) lies within the shrine precinct and is believed to be inhabited by a {{ill|Dragon god|ja|龍神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/dragon god|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1206058}}.<ref name="ic"/> Historically connected to the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|en|Miya River (Mie)|qid=Q6884164|lt=Miyagawa River}} and {{ill|Seta River (Mie)|en|Seta River (Mie)|qid=Q7456322|lt=Setagawa River}}, it influenced the naming of the "Funae" area.<ref name="ic"/>

== History ==
While the exact founding date is unknown, Kawarabuchi Shrine appears in the "Toyōke Daijingū Ritual Records" compiled in 804 (Enryaku 23), indicating its ancient origins.<ref name="sk"/> It was reconstructed in the Edo period and relocated in 1878 due to flood risks.<ref name="sk"/>

== Festivals ==
Annual festivals include the {{ill|Reisai|ja|例祭|fr|Reisai}} on September 15 and a {{ill|Shinto ritual|ja|神事|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinji (ritual)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11588671}} on March 1.<ref name="uy5"/> The "Fuchi Festival" involves {{ill|Kagura|en|Kagura|qid=Q1348260|lt=kagura}} performances and ritual offerings floated on Oboro Pond.<ref name="uy5"/>

== Access ==
* Public transport: From {{ill|Iseshi Station|en|Iseshi Station|qid=Q6079748|lt=Ise Station}}, take a {{ill|Mie Kotsu|en|Mie Kotsu|qid=Q6843516|lt=Mie Kotsu}} bus to "Asahidori" stop, then a 3-minute walk.
* By car: 8 minutes north from {{ill|Ise-nishi itnerchange|ja|伊勢西インターチェンジ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Nishi IC|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10884865}} on {{ill|Mie Prefectural Road Route 32|ja|三重県道32号伊勢磯部線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 32|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11357920}}.
